body.statement: At \(\omega_0\), the optimizer set \(\mathcal G(\omega_0)\) of the internally chosen functional \(G_{\omega_0}\) is a singleton. For its unique element \(r\), outward-rounded certificates establish \(L_{\omega_0}(r)>0.1965\) and \(L_{\omega_0}(r_{\mathrm{alt}}(\omega_0))<0.18453\). Thus minimizing the scalar maximum of the three pairwise marginal contrast variances does not determine a Gaussian minimax-regret-optimal design: every minimizer of \(L_{\omega_0}\) differs from that \(r\), with certified regret gap exceeding \(0.01197\) relative to the displayed feasible alternative.
body.justification: The theorem positively identifies a feature of correlated three-policy regret geometry that the scalar maximum pairwise-variance summary does not preserve.
body.gap: The inspected Gaussian treatment-choice and annotation results do not give an exact open-region example in which two designs ordered by a self-contained pairwise-variance probe are strictly reversed by the full overlapping-policy regret game.
body.consumer: For CodiEtAl2025ClinicalRules and KimEtAl2025AzithromycinRules, prospective independent validation of the frozen ABCD azithromycin policy menu can use the internal \(G_\omega\) probe to diagnose whether a covariance summary retains enough joint information for the validation design. Neither cited paper is claimed to use or recommend \(G_\omega\).
body.proof_tex:
At \(\omega_0\), the fourth stratum has \(d_4=0\), while \(d_1=(1,0)^\top\), \(d_2=(0,1)^\top\), and \(d_3=(1,1)^\top\). Symmetrizing the two arm rates within a stratum preserves annotation cost and, by strict convexity of \(r\mapsto1/r\), weakly decreases each stratum's covariance coefficient. With symmetric useful-stratum rates write
\[
a=\frac{0.03}{r_1},\qquad b=\frac{0.30}{r_2},\qquad c=\frac{0.25}{r_3};
\quad
\Sigma=\begin{pmatrix}a+c&c\\c&b+c\end{pmatrix},
\quad G=\max\{a+c,b+c,a+b\}.
\]
Put \(\alpha=9/634\). The supporting objective
\[
H_\alpha=\alpha(a+b)+(1-\alpha)(b+c)
\]
is no larger than \(G\). It is strictly convex in all six useful arm rates. Its budget-constrained first-order equations, with the agreement-stratum rates at their floor, have the unique solution
\[
s=\frac{\sqrt{634}}{25},\qquad
r_{3G}=\frac{529/1000}{317/1250+(3/10)s},\qquad
r_{2G}=sr_{3G},\qquad r_{1G}=\frac3{25}r_{3G},\qquad r_{4G}=\frac1{20}.
\]
At this point \(a=c<b\), so \(H_\alpha=a+b=b+c=G\). Thus the lower bound \(H_\alpha\le G\) is attained at its unique minimizer. Strict convexity, including the equality condition in arm symmetrization, proves that the full eight-coordinate optimizer set \(\mathcal G(\omega_0)\) is the singleton consisting of this arm-symmetric design.

For the regret lower certificate use the prior with atoms
\[
(-5/8,-5/8),\quad(0,5/8),\quad(5/8,0)
\]
and weights \((13/40,7/20,13/40)\). At each atom every incorrect action has regret \(5/8\). If \(P_{kk}\) is the probability that the Gaussian Bayes discriminant selects the correct atom, its Bayes risk is
\[
B_G=\frac58\left(1-\sum_kw_kP_{kk}\right)\le L_{\omega_0}(r_G).
\]
Writing \(\beta_k=\Sigma(r_G)^{-1}h^k\) and \(b_k=\log w_k-(h^k)^\top\Sigma(r_G)^{-1}h^k/2\), each \(P_{kk}\) is the probability of two affine Gaussian inequalities. Direct differentiation of the bivariate normal integral in its correlation parameter gives
\[
\Phi_2(u,v;q)=\Phi(u)\Phi(v)+\int_0^q\phi_2(u,v;t)\,dt.
\]
For \(|t|\le q_*<1\), diagonalization and \(\sup_z z^2e^{-z^2/2}=2/e\) give
\[
|\partial_t\phi_2(u,v;t)|
\le\frac{q_*+2/e}{2\pi(1-q_*^2)^{3/2}}.
\]
Thus \(N\)-panel midpoint quadrature has outward error at most \(q_*^2\) times this bound divided by \(4N\). With \(N=512\) and 96-bit outward interval arithmetic, the resulting rational-endpoint enclosure proves \(B_G>0.1965\).

For the feasible alternative, exact arithmetic gives
\[
\sum_xp_xr^0_{\mathrm{alt},x}=\frac{11}{20},\qquad
\Sigma(r^0_{\mathrm{alt}})=
\begin{pmatrix}433/1205&125/482\\125/482&8695/14942\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Use the feasible rule selecting the largest of \(z_1,z_2,0\). Its selection probabilities are bivariate normal quadrant probabilities, so the same identity with \(N=64\) encloses its risk. On a square of sup-norm half-width \(w\), the state-risk modulus is
\[
2+\frac{\sqrt2}{\sqrt{\lambda_{\min}\{\Sigma(r^0_{\mathrm{alt}})\}}}.
\]
An outward-rounded dyadic cover of \([-1,1]^2\), with \(74107\) accepted leaves and maximum depth ten, gives the global upper enclosure
\[
\sup_{h\in[-1,1]^2}R(h)<0.184529576390235<0.18453.
\]
All tail probabilities are full Gaussian quadrant probabilities, so no observation truncation is hidden. The finite interval operations are certified by \(\mathrm{thm:certified\text{-}computation}\). Therefore
\[
L_{\omega_0}(r_G)>0.1965,\qquad
L_{\omega_0}(r_{\mathrm{alt}}(\omega_0))<0.18453,
\]
and the regret gap exceeds \(0.1965-0.18453=0.01197\). Since a feasible design has smaller regret, no minimizer of \(L_{\omega_0}\) equals the unique \(G\)-minimizer.
